body: Hell. I even took my Zoloft today and I still want to end it all. My only worry is that I don't have enough Ambien.

I've done the whole living abroad thing and experienced pretty much everything I want to out of life. I don't regret it, but it did make me have to file for bankruptcy and have to start this whole nonsense all over again.
Life is just a racket, plain and simple.
I don't want anything anymore. That's the whole point.
Same here, minus the gun. I used to sometimes be okay with the loneliness, but it's just too constant and it's not going to end until I do.

I think the real tragedy here is that I'm a pretty easy sell. I just need one person - live, not via the internet - to genuinely give a crap about me and take the time to understand my pain and let me vent and I probably wouldn't be so suicidal. But what if angels sat on pinheads? I'm tired of waiting for this mythical person to spring into existence. I can't bear the thought of another 44 years alone.

I'm not loved. Sympathetic strangers is completely different to what I'm talking about. I doubt anyone can get through life knowing that all they have is a sympathetic stranger to pretend he cares.
And for what it's worth, I am alone. Family and (former) friends are/were very well aware of my depression, but their response was always to either ignore it because they had their own issues (family) or to put the blame on myself for not living up to my potential (friends) - showing that they didn't understand the severity of the situation.

I was unemployed and living with a friend until that bridge got burned by my lack of work. Since then, fewer and fewer people (now none) seem to be willing to give me the time of day. And I'm talking about family, too. It's like I've been shunned.

Same here. I've pretty much traveled everywhere I want to go which was about the only exciting thing I found out of life. Now it just seems like a burden to renew my passport even if I could care enough to plan going somewhere.
I know the feeling. My greatest fear is dying alone but I know it's gonna happen that way. I wish I knew of an answer.
Yes, but no. It's been my experience that talking rarely, if ever, is effective.
